builders.name: Aaron Levie
builders.summary_en: He estimates that meaningful use of AI agents in enterprise workflows remains extremely limited, despite the attention they receive. His less-than-1% figure is presented as an estimate, not a measured statistic.
builders.summary_zh: 他估计，尽管 AI 智能体受到广泛关注，企业工作流程中的实质性部署仍很少。低于 1% 是他的估计，并非帖文提供的实测数据。

slang.definition_en: AI systems that can carry out multi-step tasks with some autonomy.
slang.definition_zh: 能以一定自主性执行多步骤任务的 AI 系统。

slang.definition_en: Recurring processes used to run a business.
slang.definition_zh: 企业日常运营中反复执行的工作流程。

keywords.definition_zh: 企业内部为完成业务任务而执行的一系列流程。
keywords.example_zh: 他认为绝大多数企业业务流程尚未真正用上智能体；文中的不到1%是他的估计。

keywords.definition_zh: 能够围绕目标执行任务、调用工具或推进多个步骤的 AI 系统。
keywords.example_zh: 他讨论的是智能体在企业流程中的实际应用程度，并认为其普及远低于外界关注度所暗示的水平。

tweets.text:
This is correct. The vast majority of enterprise workflows have not actually had agents applied to them in any meaningful way. The economy probably has this deployed < 1% right now.

At best you have a few automated systems in a company that do a single pass of an LLM to make a decision or provide feedback, but very little real “automation”. Some of this is a statement about the adoption rates of technology in enterprises, but the vast majority of it is really just due to the capability of AI itself.

That’s all changing. Now with computer use, long running agents, harness improvements and surrounding infrastructure, we’re finally at a point where we can start to apply agents at more complex workflows. 

We will see self-improving systems that can take any particular workflow goal and improve the execution rates over a volume of instances. And with the emerging form factor of agent swarms, you can just choose to deploy any amount of compute at a problem and agents will off and do the work.

This won’t be about and users prompting agents to complete a specific task for them, but instead the organization reengineering the underlying workflows to take advantage of agents in their processes. This will have a massive impact in finance, life sciences, healthcare, and other information-heavy domains. Lots of opportunity to build and deploy these systems right now.
tweets.summary_en: Meaningful enterprise agent adoption remains minimal, largely because of AI capability limits, but advances in computer use, long-running agents, and infrastructure are opening up complex workflow automation. The biggest opportunity is redesigning organizational processes around self-improving agents and agent swarms, especially in information-heavy industries.

slang_glossary.definition_zh: 软件开发口语，指改动或功能已经合入或交付；不一定表示已向所有用户开放。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Annual recurring revenue: a yearly measure of recurring subscription or contract revenue.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 年度经常性收入，衡量订阅或合同带来的持续性收入，不等于利润。

slang_glossary.definition_en: In hiring, concrete evidence of ability through completed work or projects.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 在招聘中指通过实际成果或项目证明能力；此处不是区块链中的工作量证明机制。

slang_glossary.definition_en: The original project or repository whose changes can flow into a derived version.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 上游项目或代码仓库，其更新可以被整合进衍生版本。

slang_glossary.definition_en: AI systems that carry out programming tasks using tools and multiple steps.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 通过调用工具和执行多个步骤完成编程任务的 AI 智能体。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Human-computer interaction: the study and design of how people interact with computers.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 人机交互，研究和设计人与计算机之间的交互方式。

slang_glossary.definition_en: AI at or near the leading edge of available capabilities.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 能力处于或接近当前领先水平的前沿 AI。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Models below the leading capability tier, often offering different cost or speed tradeoffs.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 能力低于最前沿梯队的模型，通常在成本或速度上提供不同取舍。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A derogatory term for low-quality, often mass-produced AI content.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 对低质量、往往批量生成的 AI 内容的贬称。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A JavaScript and TypeScript toolkit that includes a runtime and development tools.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 面向 JavaScript 和 TypeScript 的工具套件，包含运行时和开发工具。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A file containing instructions for building a Docker container image.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 包含 Docker 容器镜像构建指令的文件。

slang_glossary.definition_en: In AI, systems that take actions through tools to pursue a task or goal.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 在 AI 语境中，指能借助工具采取行动、推进任务或目标的智能体。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Sequences of business tasks and approvals used within organizations.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 企业内部用于完成业务任务和审批的工作流程。

slang_glossary.definition_en: The quantity of text-processing units a model consumes or generates.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 模型处理或生成的词元数量，常用于衡量用量和计算费用。

slang_glossary.definition_en: The elapsed time between starting a task and receiving its result.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 从发起任务到收到结果所经过的时间。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A metaphor for an organized, highly automated system of software production.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 软件工厂，比喻组织化、高度自动化的软件生产体系。

slang_glossary.definition_en: In startup finance, a reduction in an owner’s percentage stake when additional shares are issued.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 股权稀释，指发行新增股份后原股东持股比例下降。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Failure to act because of excessive analysis or comparison.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 分析瘫痪，指因过度分析或比较而迟迟无法行动。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A long span of time or many linked steps over which a system must plan and act.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 长时间跨度或多步骤任务范围，要求系统持续规划和行动。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Describing inputs or situations that differ from a model’s training distribution.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 分布外，指输入或情境偏离模型训练数据的分布。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An informal measure of useful AI capability relative to electrical power consumption.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 每瓦智能，以耗电功率衡量 AI 有效能力的非正式说法，并非统一标准指标。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Reinforcement learning settings in which agents act and receive feedback or rewards.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 强化学习环境，智能体在其中采取行动并获得反馈或奖励。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Describing technical staff who work closely with customers to implement solutions.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 前线部署的，通常指深入客户现场或业务场景、协助落地解决方案的技术人员。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Business shorthand for slide presentations, especially pitches or briefings.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 商业口语中的演示文稿，常指融资路演或业务汇报幻灯片。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A meme-like phrase used to pivot abruptly into self-promotion.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 一种带有网络梗意味的表达，用来突然转向自我宣传，字面意思是「总之，这是我的 SoundCloud」。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Slang for missing or mishandling a potentially lucrative opportunity.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 错失或搞砸赚钱机会；「bag」在这里指金钱或潜在收益。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A dismissive phrase suggesting something is minor or unimpressive.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 小儿科；用轻蔑或调侃的语气表示某事不算什么。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Short for laughing out loud; often signals humor, irony, or softened tone.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 「笑出声」的缩写，也常用于表达调侃、反讽或缓和语气。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A vulgar abbreviation of fuck my life, expressing frustration or regret.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 粗俗表达「fuck my life」的缩写，用来宣泄懊恼、沮丧或后悔。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An informal written abbreviation of because.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: because 的非正式书面缩写，意为「因为」。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An informal spelling of would’ve, meaning would have.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: would’ve 的非正式拼写，即 would have，常用于描述未发生的假设情况。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An informal spelling of little, often conveying a casual or affectionate tone.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: little 的非正式拼写，常带有随意或亲切的语气。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Initial public offering: a company’s first offering of shares to the public.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 首次公开募股，即公司首次向公众发行股票。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Command-line interface: a way to operate software through typed commands.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 命令行界面，通过输入文本命令操作软件。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A programming language that extends JavaScript with a type system.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 在 JavaScript 基础上加入类型系统的编程语言。

slang_glossary.definition_en: In this context, the AI coding product or the company behind it.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 此处指 AI 编程产品 Cursor 或其背后的公司。

slang_glossary.definition_en: The name of xAI’s AI assistant.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: xAI 旗下 AI 助手的名称。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An automated software account or program that performs tasks or responds to users.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 自动执行任务或回应用户的软件程序或账号。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Software whose license permits access to, modification of, and redistribution of its source code.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 开源软件，其许可证允许访问、修改和再分发源代码。

slang_glossary.definition_en: The underlying components and mechanisms of an operating system.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 操作系统底层的内部组件和运作机制。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Unusual or boundary situations that may reveal failures in a system.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 边界情况或少见情境，可能暴露系统缺陷。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Designed around AI capabilities as a central part of the product.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: AI 原生的，指以 AI 能力为核心进行产品设计。

slang_glossary.definition_en: The macOS interface area used to access apps and switch between them.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: macOS 的程序坞，用于访问应用和切换应用。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Short practical assignments or work periods used to assess a candidate’s ability.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 工作试做，通过短期实际任务或工作过程评估候选人的能力。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Pacific Standard Time, UTC minus eight hours; sometimes used loosely to mean Pacific Time.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 太平洋标准时间，即 UTC−8；日常表达中有时被宽泛地用来指太平洋时间。
